questions.question: A sum, when invested at 20% simple interest per annum, amounts to ₹4,800 after 3 years. What is the simple interest (in ₹) on the same sum at the same rate in 1 year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for **3 years** at **20%** = 20% × 3 = **60%**.

Total amount percentage = **Principal (100%)** + **Interest (60%)** = **160%**.

Given: 160% = **₹4,800** ⇒ 1% = 4800 ÷ 160 = **₹30**.

Interest for **1 year** at 20% = 20 × 30 = **₹600**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Amount (A) = **₹4,800**, Rate (R) = **20% p.a.**, Time (T) = **3 years**.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P + SI = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aac82e86215a1adf686fd936417f8bf15d857f0a0c13c48f6d9c5ef5953f178a.png] 

⇒ 4,800 = P × (1 + (20 × 3) ÷ 100)

⇒ 4,800 = P × (1 + 0.6)

⇒ 4,800 = P × 1.6

⇒ P = 4,800 ÷ 1.6 = **₹3,000**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = (3000 × 20 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ Simple Interest = 30 × 20 = **₹600**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI) formula

SI is calculated only on the **Principal** amount: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is principal, R is rate per annum, and T is time in years.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total **Amount (A)** is the sum of the Principal and Simple Interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Annual Interest Constant

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains **constant every year** because it is always calculated on the original principal.

questions.question: When the difference between compound interest, compounded annually, and simple interest for three years is ₹228 at 4% interest per annum, the principal is ₹_____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **3-year period**, the difference (D) between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** is given by the formula:

D = P × (r/100)² × (3 + r/100)

Given: D = ₹228 and r = 4%.

⇒ 228 = P × (4/100)² × (3 + 4/100)

⇒ 228 = P × (1/625) × (304/100)

⇒ P = (228 × 625 × 100) / 304 = 46875

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46,875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Rate (R)** = 4% per annum

**Difference (CI − SI)** = ₹228

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b97aeb3bbf5a07d15b16e8bcc8d34294e69ec8db4934f2b20a8af8cb60d0322.png] 

Let the **Principal** be P.

**Simple Interest (SI)** for 3 years:

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ SI = (P × 4 × 3) / 100 = 12P / 100

**Compound Interest (CI)** for 3 years:

⇒ Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

⇒ A = P(1 + 4/100)³ = P(1 + 1/25)³ = P(26/25)³

⇒ A = P(17576 / 15625)

⇒ CI = A − P = P(17576/15625 − 1) = 1951P / 15625

According to the question, **CI − SI = 228**:

⇒ 1951P / 15625 − 12P / 100 = 228

⇒ (1951P × 4 − 12P × 625) / 62500 = 228

⇒ (7804P − 7500P) / 62500 = 228

⇒ 304P / 62500 = 228

⇒ P = (228 × 62500) / 304

⇒ P = 3/4 × 62500 = 3 × 15625 = 46875

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46,875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 2 years

The difference between CI and SI for a 2-year period is given by D = P(r/100)².

Effective Rate Method

For CI of 2 years, effective rate = r + r + (r×r)/100. For 3 years, apply the successive formula again.

Simple Interest Property

Simple Interest remains the same for every year if the principal and rate are constant.

questions.question: A bank offers 7.4% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits ₹8,022 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ______ (give your answer correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Half-yearly rate** (r) = 7.4% ÷ 2 = **3.7%**

Interest on 1st deposit (2 cycles) = 3.7 + 3.7 + (3.7 × 3.7)/100 = **7.5369%**

Interest on 2ⁿd deposit (1 cycle) = **3.7%**

**Total Interest %** = 7.5369% + 3.7% = **11.2369%**

Interest amount = 8022 × 11.2369 / 100 = **₹901.42**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹901.42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹8,022** for each deposit

Annual Rate (R) = **7.4%** | Time = **1 year**

Compounding = **Half-yearly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47108003f9aadb68d4fc6cea09cc14c1719293f8e1e9a7fa1cfaed4862b67712.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest (CI) = P × [(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1]

Where r = R/2 and n = number of half-years.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 7.4 ÷ 2 = 3.7%

⇒ **Interest on 1st deposit** (for 2 half-years):

⇒ I₁ = 8022 × [(1 + 3.7/100)² − 1]

⇒ I₁ = 8022 × [(1.037)² − 1] = 8022 × [1.075369 − 1]

⇒ I₁ = 8022 × 0.075369 = 604.610118

⇒ **Interest on 2ⁿd deposit** (for 1 half-year):

⇒ I₂ = 8022 × [3.7/100] = 8022 × 0.037

⇒ I₂ = 296.814

⇒ **Total Interest** = I₁ + I₂ = 604.610118 + 296.814

⇒ Total Interest = 901.424118 ≈ ₹901.42

**∴ The correct answer is ₹901.42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate r per period over n periods, the effective rate is [(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1] × 100%.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 and the time periods are doubled.

Successive Percentage Shortcut

For two periods with rate x%, total interest % = x + x + (x²/100).

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,000 at 6% per annum rate of interest for the period from 3 February 2023 to 17 April 2023.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the total days: **Feb (25) + Mar (31) + Apr (17) = 73 days**.

Since 73 days is exactly **1/5** of a year (73/365), calculate 1/5 of the annual interest.

Annual Interest = 6% of ₹2,000 = ₹120.

Simple Interest for the period = 120 ÷ 5 = **₹24**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹2,000**

Rate (R) = **6% per annum**

Period: **3 February 2023** to **17 April 2023**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88219710fae221590b332de528c817a1f19e7b211de52b07af76ab3537616a13.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of days in February = 28 − 3 = **25 days** (2023 is a non-leap year)

⇒ Number of days in March = **31 days**

⇒ Number of days in April = **17 days**

⇒ Total days (T) = 25 + 31 + 17 = **73 days**

⇒ Time in years = 73 ÷ 365 = **1/5 year**

⇒ SI = (2000 × 6 × 1/5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2000 × 6) ÷ 500

⇒ SI = 4 × 6 = **24**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time Calculation for Interest

While calculating the number of days, the day on which money is deposited is usually excluded and the day on which money is withdrawn is included.

Standard Year vs Leap Year

For interest calculations, a standard year is taken as 365 days. If the year is a leap year (divisible by 4), February has 29 days.

Relationship between Amount and SI

The total **Amount (A)** repaid after the period is the sum of the **Principal (P)** and the **Simple Interest (SI)**: A = P + SI.

**Effective interest rate** for 3 years = 20% × 3 = 60%

**Total Amount** = 100% (Principal) + 60% (Interest) = 160%

Given 160% → ₹8,640, so 1% = 8640 ÷ 160 = ₹54

**Interest for 2 years** = 20% × 2 = 40%

**Simple Interest (2 yrs)** = 40 × 54 = ₹2,160

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,160.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Amount (A) = **₹8,640**, Rate (R) = **20% p.a.**, Time (T₁) = **3 years**, Time (T₂) = **2 years**.

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + RT/100) and SI = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/020a11d1d3f8386140a58f3bbeec9a7a74ae2a1798251954aeb737e5093597b3.png] 

⇒ Amount = P + (P × 20 × 3) / 100

⇒ 8640 = P + 0.6P

⇒ 8640 = 1.6P

⇒ P = 8640 ÷ 1.6 = **₹5,400**

⇒ SI (for 2 years) = (5400 × 20 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 54 × 40 = **₹2,160**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,160.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest remains constant for every year if the principal and rate are unchanged. SI for 'n' years = n × (SI for 1 year).

Effective Rate Method

Total interest percentage = (Rate × Time)%. This can be directly added to 100% to find the Amount percentage.

Amount Formula

The total sum at the end of the period is A = P + SI. In terms of P, A = P(1 + RT/100).

questions.question: If at the same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest, compounded annually, is 41, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Difference (D)** between **CI** and **SI** for 2 years = 41 − 40 = ₹1

**SI** for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

**Rate (R)** = (Difference ÷ SI of 1 year) × 100 = (1 ÷ 20) × 100 = 5%

**Principal (P)** = (SI of 1 year × 100) ÷ R = (20 × 100) ÷ 5 = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Simple Interest (SI)** for 2 years = ₹40

Total **Compound Interest (CI)** for 2 years = ₹41

Time (T) = 2 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51039f7f9411d69e50fb27695726aad330858cf5b4479725f71633160c833dc9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1st year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ In **Compound Interest**, the interest for the 1st year is the same as **SI** = ₹20

⇒ **CI** for the 2ⁿd year = Total **CI** − 1st year interest = 41 − 20 = ₹21

⇒ The extra ₹1 (21 − 20) is the interest earned on the 1st year interest (₹20)

⇒ **Rate of Interest (R)** = (1 ÷ 20) × 100 = 5% per annum

⇒ Now, using **SI** formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 40 = (P × 5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 40 = (P × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ 40 = P ÷ 10

⇒ P = 40 × 10 = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The difference (D) is given by the formula D = P(R ÷ 100)².

Ratio of CI and SI for 2 Years

The relationship is expressed as CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200.

Effective Rate for Compound Interest

For a rate R% for 2 years, the effective CI rate is R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.
